significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(ii) causal decomposition: a separable “surface-trigger shortcut” directly drives over-refusal while harmfulness belief primarily drives justified refusal, and selectively suppressing the former preserves the latter. This is more constraining than the median refusal-direction hypothesis because it assigns two independently manipulable contributors to two behavioral regimes, informing why interventions against the single refusal direction characterized by Arditi et al. (NeurIPS 2024) can conflate safety with excessive refusal; it establishes both the over-refusal phenomenon and a definite internal mechanism. Verified false would still rule out lexical bypass as the dominant explanation of cases benchmarked by XSTest and OR-Bench, although it would not identify the alternative mechanism; true and false are distinguishable because the claim specifically asserts dominant trigger-path mediation with low harmfulness-belief activation. Topic substitution fails: generic “mechanistic LLM safety” would not earn this score, whereas the quoted three-way decomposition adds a consequential, non-default distinction.

reach.justification: The concrete handle is the “trigger-salience component of the residual stream” and the associated intervention that “ablates only the trigger-salience component ... while preserving harmfulness belief”; it is ex ante with respect to refusal because it can alter inference before the model emits its answer, giving deployers an action window. The hypothesis asserts a reusable qualitative decomposition across over-refusal cases and model families, but after per-model re-extraction it does not predict a quantitative threshold or effect size, so much of what transfers is the intervention recipe rather than a law about the next model. Its downstream users could include model auditors and deployers seeking to reduce false refusals without weakening genuine safety, though lexical-trigger dependence and the expressly untested frontier-model scope limit broader transfer. Topic substitution fails: the named selective inference-time control, rather than the general safety topic, supports the above-median reach.
